memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. Brockhaus Technologies (BKHT-DE), Triaging record dated 2026-10-12 at EUR17.60. The case is a sum-of-the-parts and reinvestment case dressed as a corporate change: the company sold the business that was 89 percent of its revenue (Bikeleasing), holds about EUR140m of net cash after a EUR90m tender, one sub-scale secure-KVM hardware unit (IHSE) and a two-person head office that has promised to return about EUR180m in total and buy the next platform with the rest. The shares trade below our mid-point net cash of EUR20.6 a share, so the holder is paid to own the stub; the modal return is 12.0 percent a year over eighteen months and 10.8 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar. The park rule applies and the record does not argue against it: business quality (E 2, BB 2) is D and trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) is D, two of the four gates. The case moves from park to progress on either of two things: the price below about EUR15.9 with the second return proposed (the modal path then clears 20 percent a year from cash alone); or the H2 2026 revenue step delivered on 12-Nov-26 and in the FY2026 results together with a first acquisition at or below 8x EBITDA and under EUR100m of enterprise value, funded from cash (the deployment branch then becomes modal at 18 to 19 percent a year). It moves from park to bearish on a debt- or paper-funded acquisition above EUR150m of enterprise value, or on a 2027 AGM notice with no distribution. The first fact to verify is the EUR28.7m tax question on the disposal gain.
case: The thesis. Brockhaus Technologies is a sum-of-the-parts and reinvestment case dressed as a corporate change. It has sold the business that was 89 percent of its revenue and is now about EUR140m of net cash, one sub-scale secure-KVM hardware unit and a two-person head office that has promised to hand back about EUR180m in total and buy the next platform with the rest. At EUR17.60 the shares trade below our mid-point net cash of EUR20.6 a share, so the holder is paid to own what is left; but the modal return, a probable second cash return of EUR13.2 a share plus the stub re-rated to about its cash, is 12 percent a year against the 20 percent bar, and the case is not compelling at this price.

The internal change is among the strongest in form the screen describes and has already happened. Six of twelve internal forces are strong and dated: perimeter reduction A (Palas sold November 2022 for up to EUR76m; Bikeleasing sold; kvm-tec deconsolidated January 2026; desktop KVM exited; about EUR300m of divestment proceeds against EUR120m invested); shareholder returns A (the EUR90m tender; about EUR90m more intended; the EUR180m is about 150 percent of the post-tender market capitalisation); balance sheet B (net debt to net cash; the EUR183m reserves transfer; the one thing undone is the IHSE loan due 31-Dec-26); other leaders B (the whole IHSE leadership replaced; an acquisitions specialist from Volaris; the auditor replaced after a seven-firm tender); standards B (IHSE operating-expense ratio from 81 percent of sales in Q4 2024 to 63 percent in Q4 2025; other operating expenses -45 percent in H1 2026; managing director dismissed after the misstatement); strategy C (changed in fact to a cash-rich single-platform vehicle; the forward strategy is the same acquisition model with a widened range, enterprise value EUR30m to EUR300m from EUR20m to EUR200m, and no named pipeline; the chief executive said on 18-May-26 there was no plan so far). The one red flag that applies in form, selling the crown jewel, was a sale above the market's valuation of the whole group. Acquisitions D (mooted, resourced, unexecuted; the record on kept assets is IHSE goodwill impaired EUR40m, kvm-tec insolvent, the EUR8.2m Palas earn-out written to zero; the deal record before the listing strong, 360T at 6.3x); guidance raised F (FY2025 mid-term targets of EUR290m to EUR320m at a 40 percent margin suspended March 2025; FY2024 missed on revenue EUR205m against EUR220m to EUR240m and EBITDA EUR66m against EUR80m to EUR90m; FY2025 adjusted EBITDA EUR46m missed EUR50m to EUR55m; FY2026 held, not raised); chief executive change D (none at the parent; the founder's 23, 26 and 33 percent IRR across three fund generations is the resource the case relies on). 'Internal forces' B; not A because the redeployment force has produced nothing beyond a target range and the head office is ten people.

The external forces are mixed and net down on IHSE's revenue line ('External forces' C). Defence: European NATO equipment spending projected +30 percent to $247bn in 2026; defence 43 percent of IHSE's FY2025 revenue from about 20 percent; NATO catalogue listing, Common Criteria EAL4+ and NIAP PP4 obtained over three years. Political and regulatory B: NIS2, the NATO 5 percent of GDP guideline by 2032, German export controls raising entry barriers, a sovereign-procurement preference; against, the same export controls deny or delay permissions for non-NATO and Middle East destinations, and the procurement reform excludes defence until 2029. Demand C: defence up structurally, commercial KVM down structurally, the two cancelling in FY2025 and H1 2026; the Q1 2026 deferral on component supply pushed into H2 is the base for the implied acceleration. Competition D: Vertiv's Avocent MergePoint Unity 2 with FIPS 140-3 in early 2026; Adder faster on IP-based KVM; Belden's Thinklogical the largest defence competitor; primes capturing the integration layer; the six-player, about-10-percent-each structure of a EUR300m market unchanged; IHSE's 75.5 percent gross margin above Adder's 66 percent five-year average. Disruption D: software-defined routing and virtual sessions strengthening; kvm-tec's bankruptcy the realised instance; hardware-enforced isolation protects only the certified niche, where NIAP PP4 is a mandatory threshold. Revenue cycle D: three years of decline; the turn only implied by guidance. Macro D: German stagnation weighs on commercial EMEA; the environment reads a late-cycle rates squeeze turning into credit stress; the company is self-funded. Supply C: no component inflation; availability a live constraint; single-source secure components. Currency C: no hedges deployed 2022 to 2025; a 10 percent euro appreciation compresses earnings before tax by EUR113k; a 30 percent dollar move shifts translated Americas revenue by EUR2.46m.
counter_case: The market is right to value the stub below zero, and the case is a value trap of the kind the research calls a false friend. The head office costs about EUR5m a year and will cost it for as long as the founder searches for a platform. IHSE is a EUR30m hardware business in a market that software is hollowing out from below, with four customers at 48 percent of revenue, an Americas that fell 65 percent in a half on a policy it does not control, a margin of 14.8 percent only because costs were cut and not because anything was sold, and a new chief executive whose first half showed no revenue visibility. The second return is a stated intention from a man who said five weeks before closing that he had no plan, and who at the same time raised his acquisition ceiling to EUR300m of enterprise value, which with EUR50m of retained cash means debt or paper. The founder's record on assets he kept is two write-downs and a zero. The sell-side has left. The register is illiquid and will be more so after the tender. The environment is against small single-case names, with Fragility at Double Underweight and strengthened this week. The EUR28.7m tax question could put the low-end cash within 3 percent of the price, so even the cover is thin. On that reading the right value for the stub ex-cash is the cost of the head office for five years, about -EUR25m, and the right price is net cash less that, about EUR17, which is where the shares are. The research's own pre-mortem gives its bear scenario a 75 to 90 percent cumulative failure probability over eighteen to twenty-four months, its failure clusters are correlated at about 0.75, its probability-weighted downside on the old perimeter was EUR8 to EUR15 a share, and its own joint probability for the bull case was 33.6 percent; a thesis whose own research gives the bull case one-in-three odds is not a B.

Against the D at Building Block level, the opposite counter-case is also carried at full force. The framework's earnings chain is the wrong lens for a liquidation-plus-option case: the holder at EUR17.60 buys EUR18.2 to EUR22.5 of net cash, of which EUR13.2 is to be handed back within eighteen months, plus IHSE, a 75 percent gross-margin certified defence supplier in a EUR300m oligopoly niche with new leadership, plus the founder's option to buy the next Bikeleasing, for less than nothing; the thesis is highly material and the outputs that matter, cash per share and the discount, are improving. The foundation is a capital allocator with three fund generations at rising IRRs, two exits at 2.5x and 4x, a 22.4 percent stake, a sale at 11x of what the market valued at less, and a tender at a 42 percent premium to today's price; IHSE is a sideshow worth EUR30m to EUR40m either way and its control failures were small in money and fixed fast. 'Major CfC Clearing' fits better than D: the concern was major and is clearing on hard evidence (clean opinions; new leadership; margin up 4.4 points; costs down 45 percent), the estimates and guidance are cut to the floor, the sell-side has capitulated, and the quality floor should be read on IHSE's advantages rather than one loss-making year. The case is close to riskless on a three-year view, the riskiness attributes measure a stub that is a small part of the value, and the framework's D over-weights operating risk where the operating business is a free option.
triggers: - The EUR28.7m tax question on the disposal gain: whether the 30-Jun-26 net cash of EUR243.0m is before or after it; the first fact to verify. At the low end the cover of the market capitalisation is 1.04x and the discount at EUR17.60 is 3 percent, not 14 percent; Invalidate level: net cash after tax and tender below EUR120m.
- The tender result (closed 9-Oct-26, unpublished): completion above 80 percent is the test; below it is an Alarm and breaks the 6.81m share-count arithmetic.

- The second cash return: a distribution resolution in the 2027 AGM notice. No proposal by the 2027 AGM notice is an Alarm; a 2027 AGM notice with no distribution moves the recommendation from park to bearish. The price below about EUR15.9 with the second return proposed moves it from park to progress.

- The deployment: no letter of intent by the end of Q1 2027 is an Alarm and pushes the announcement condition from probable to plausible; an acquisition above EUR150m of enterprise value or funded with debt invalidates the discipline condition and moves the recommendation to bearish; a first acquisition at or below 8x EBITDA, under EUR100m of enterprise value, funded from cash, together with the H2 2026 revenue step, moves it to progress.

- IHSE revenue: the Q3 2026 statement on 12-Nov-26 (IHSE below EUR8m for the quarter changes our mind on FY2026); the Americas below EUR2.5m a quarter for two quarters is an Alarm; FY2026 revenue guidance cut below EUR28m is the Invalidate level; H2 2026 needs EUR16.6m to EUR18.6m.

- IHSE margin: two consecutive quarters above a 20 percent adjusted EBITDA margin with revenue growing would make 'Major CfC Clearing' the primary at C or better and say the stub is worth more than we give it; a margin back at about 10 percent takes the 'Modal return' from D to F.
